title: Normalized finite open external-tensor comparison
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F_{p^a}}$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,m}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$ for $m\geq1$. Use a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum] with its specified canonical exchange and projection transformations [def-exchange-projection, def-sf-pf]. All schemes below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes and all morphisms are separated of finite type. Integral pullbacks and tensors are completed; field operations use rationalization and common finite stages. Fix finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $\bar X\to B$, $\bar Y\to B$ be morphisms and let $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Y\hookrightarrow\bar Y$ be open immersions. Put $\bar T=\bar X\times_B\bar Y$, $T=X\times_BY$, and $u=j\times_Bk:T\hookrightarrow\bar T$, with projections $\bar p,\bar q$ on $\bar T$ and $p,q$ on $T$. For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, set $D=Lp^*K\otimes^LLq^*L$. The canonical open base-change maps and open projection transformations determine a natural isomorphism
$$e_{j,k}:L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes^LL\bar q^*k_!L\xrightarrow{\sim}u_!D$$
whose restriction along $u$ is the identity of $D$. More precisely, factor $u=j_1k_1$ through $X\times_B\bar Y$. Open base change of $j$, projection formula for $j_1$, open base change of $k$, and projection formula for $k_1$ (using the signed symmetry to put its extension factor first), followed by $j_{1!}k_{1!}\cong u_!$, give this isomorphism. The construction using the opposite factorization through $\bar X\times_BY$ gives the same map. Under a swap of factors, the maps $e_{j,k}$ intertwine the signed external tensor symmetries. For any third open immersion $l:W\hookrightarrow\bar W$ over $B$ and $M\in D^b_{ctf}(W,\Lambda)$, the two composites built from $e$ on $\bar X\times_B\bar Y\times_B\bar W$ agree after the canonical associators and normalized composition identifications of extension by zero. Both restrict to the identity on $K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$, where $\boxtimes$ means tensor of the projection pullbacks.

proof.text: Use the finite constant ring $A=A_{E,n}$ throughout, on the ambient ordinary pro-etale derived categories. For every open $v$, write $\eta^v:1\xrightarrow{\sim}v^*v_!$ for the unit normalized as the identity on sections over the open. The open normalization lemma supplies these units, full faithfulness of $v_!$, and the canonical isomorphisms $\beta$ (open base change) and $\gamma$ (open projection) whose restrictions are identities. It identifies their constant finite-coefficient specializations with the maps used in the question. Thus its hypotheses hold for every open and Cartesian square below; its objects may be arbitrary unbounded complexes, so no intermediate constructibility assertion is needed.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent argument from normalized open base change and projection

proof.text: For composable opens $w:V\hookrightarrow U$ and $v:U\hookrightarrow Z$, use the composite adjunction $v_!w_!\dashv w^*v^*$. Restriction along $vw$ is canonically $w^*v^*$, so uniqueness of left adjoints with their units gives the normalized isomorphism $c_{v,w}:v_!w_!\xrightarrow{\sim}(vw)_!$. Its restriction is the identity after the open-unit identifications: this is exactly the unit equation defining that comparison. For three opens, both composites of these comparisons carry the same pasted unit to the unit of the composite open, hence are equal by the same uniqueness. This specifies the composition identifications used below, without choosing an arbitrary scalar multiple of a composition map.

proof.text:
Put $S=X\times_B\bar Y$, with $r:S\to X$, $s:S\to\bar Y$, $j_1:S\hookrightarrow\bar T$, and $k_1:T\hookrightarrow S$. Thus $u=j_1k_1$, $rk_1=p$, and $sk_1=kq$. Set $P=Lr^*K$ and $N_0=L\bar q^*k_!L$. The square with vertical opens $j,j_1$ and horizontal projections $\bar p,r$ is Cartesian. Its $\beta$ gives $L\bar p^*j_!K\cong j_{1!}P$. Tensoring with $N_0$ and then applying $\gamma$ for $j_1$ gives
$$L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes^LN_0\longrightarrow j_{1!}P\otimes^LN_0\longrightarrow j_{1!}(P\otimes^Lj_1^*N_0)=j_{1!}(P\otimes^LLs^*k_!L).$$
The equality uses the canonical composition of pullbacks and $\bar qj_1=s$. Both arrows are natural isomorphisms by the open normalization lemma.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent argument from normalized open base change and projection

proof.text:
The square with opens $k,k_1$ and projections $s,q$ is also Cartesian. Apply its $\beta$ to obtain $Ls^*k_!L\cong k_{1!}Q$, where $Q=Lq^*L$. Inside $j_{1!}$ use the following completely typed sequence, with $\sigma$ the signed tensor symmetry:
$$P\otimes^Lk_{1!}Q\xrightarrow{\sigma}k_{1!}Q\otimes^LP\xrightarrow{\gamma_{k_1,Q,P}}k_{1!}(Q\otimes^Lk_1^*P)\xrightarrow{k_{1!}(\sigma)}k_{1!}(k_1^*P\otimes^LQ)=k_{1!}D.$$
The last equality uses $rk_1=p$. Compose with step 3 and $c_{j_1,k_1}$ of step 2. This is the asserted $e_{j,k}$ with exactly the prescribed sequence of open base changes and projection maps. Every arrow is invertible. Naturality in $K,L$ follows from naturality of $\beta,\gamma$, tensor symmetry, and the composition comparison.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent argument from normalized open base change and projection

proof.text: Restrict this composite to $T$. Each $\beta$ and $\gamma$ becomes the identity by step 1; $c_{j_1,k_1}$ becomes the identity by step 2. The two symmetries in step 4 become the symmetry of $p^*K,q^*L$ and its inverse. On homogeneous tensor sections of degrees $i,j$ their composite is multiplication by $(-1)^{ij}(-1)^{ji}=1$, so $u^*e_{j,k}=1_D$. These formulas apply to derived tensors using their K-flat total tensor models and the canonical pullback/tensor comparison: pullback preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms, and tensor descent determines the derived maps from these models. In particular restriction also preserves the associator $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ and the signed symmetry, since its tensor comparison sends the same tensor sections to the same sections. Thus all restriction identifications just used are the canonical ones, not extra choices.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent argument from normalized open base change and projection

proof.text: Let $H=L\bar p^*j_!K\otimes^LL\bar q^*k_!L$. Restriction is faithful on maps with source $H$: for $a,b:H\to u_!D'$, compose with $e_{j,k}^{-1}:u_!D\to H$. Every map $u_!D\to u_!D'$ is $u_!t$ for a unique $t:D\to D'$ by full faithfulness. Naturality of the isomorphism $\eta^u:1\to u^*u_!$ says that restriction of $u_!t$, conjugated by these units, is $t$. Hence $u^*a=u^*b$ implies $a=b$. Now perform steps 3 and 4 through $S'=\bar X\times_BY$, with $r':S'\to\bar X$, $s':S'\to Y$, $k_2=1\times k:S'\hookrightarrow\bar T$ and $j_2=j\times1:T\hookrightarrow S'$, so $u=k_2j_2$: first extend the $Y$ factor, using the Cartesian square with opens $k,k_2$ and projections $\bar q,s'$, then the $X$ factor, using the Cartesian square with opens $j,j_2$ and projections $r',p$. These are the analogous squares for $S'$, not the squares of steps 3 and 4. The construction uses the same normalized $\beta,\gamma$ of the open normalization lemma, $c_{k_2,j_2}$ of step 2, and signed symmetries placed so that each extension factor comes first before $\gamma$ is applied. Their restriction is again $1_D$ by the calculation in step 5, so this opposite-factorization map equals $e_{j,k}$.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor; agent argument from normalized open base change and projection

proof.text: Write $\tau:\bar T\cong\bar Y\times_B\bar X$ and $\tau_0:T\cong Y\times_BX$ for the swaps. Use the canonical projection-pullback identifications to bring the swapped construction back to $\bar T$, and the open base-change identification for $u$ along $\tau$ to identify its target. The required square has top map $e_{j,k}$, bottom map the transported $e_{k,j}$, left vertical map the signed external symmetry $H\to\tau^*(k_!L\boxtimes j_!K)$ and right vertical map $u_!(\sigma):u_!D\to u_!\tau_0^*(L\boxtimes K)$. On $T$ the horizontal maps are identities, the swap base-change map is the normalized identity, and both vertical maps are $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$. The two paths therefore have identical restrictions. Apply the faithful-restriction argument of step 6, with $D'=\tau_0^*(L\boxtimes K)$, to obtain equality of the paths, including their Koszul signs.

proof.text: For the third open $l$, set $v=j\times_Bk\times_Bl$, $H_3=j_!K\boxtimes k_!L\boxtimes l_!M$, and $D_3=K\boxtimes L\boxtimes M$. First apply $e_{j,k}\boxtimes1$ and then $e_{j\times k,l}$ to get $F:H_3\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!D_3$. First applying $1\boxtimes e_{k,l}$ and then $e_{j,k\times l}$ gives $G$ with the same source and target after the indicated associators. Products and projections here are over $B$; projection pullbacks preserve K-flat models by the tensor-pullback lemma. The binary construction was on all ambient complexes, so it applies also to the intermediate external products. Upon restriction to the full open, each binary map is the identity by step 5, and each composition comparison is the identity by step 2. The associators on the two sides send $((x\otimes y)\otimes z)$ to $x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ on the same K-flat tensor models; restriction does the same. Thus $v^*F=v^*G=1_{D_3}$ after these associators. Compose with $F^{-1}$ and apply full faithfulness of $v_!$ exactly as in step 6 to conclude $F=G$.
